newsitem.title: USA: Chicago TV news anchor resigns amid Springer rancor.
newsitem.headline: Chicago TV news anchor resigns amid Springer rancor.

text.p: The local NBC-TV station Thursday announced the departure of news anchor Carol Marin, the same day she criticised in a newspaper editorial the hiring of tabloid talk-show host Jerry Springer to do commentary.

Marin, who blasted Springer in the Chicago Sun-Times editorial as "the poster child for the worst television has to offer," was leaving "to pursue other interests," WMAQ-TV President and General Manager Lyle Banks said in a statement.

"Tonight's 10 p.m. newscast will be her final broadcast," Banks said. "Carol approached us earlier this year with a desire to pursue other interests and after much consideration we have chosen to honour her request."

Marin, who joined the network-owned and operated station in 1978 and was considered to be among Chicago's leading broadcast journalists, and her co-anchor Ron Magers, had openly feuded with station management since Springer was hired for nightly commentaries during the May ratings sweeps period.

In her editorial, Marin wrote that Springer lacked the credibility to deliver informed opinions in a city with a proud journalistic history epitomised by recently deceased columnist Mike Royko. She was responding to an editorial this week in which the Sun-Times called her and Magers' protests of Springer's planned commentaries "elitist."
Marin wrote that Springer's talk show dealt in "salacious" topics and aired "programs that ridicule."
"Nobody is naive here. Every working reporter knows news is a business that needs to make money to survive -- but news also is a public trust," she wrote.
Springer, a former mayor and news anchor in Cincinnati, dismissed the controversy and argued the job merely required reading a teleprompter. "It's not as if it's journalism," he said.
